html:
The 2010 Kyrgyz revolution was the uprising of April 2010 that overthrew President Kurmanbek Bakiyev of Kyrgyzstan, who had come to power in the Tulip Revolution of 2005.

Anger over corruption, his family's grip on business and sharp rises in power and heating prices led to protests in the northern town of Talas, which spread to Bishkek. On 7 April crowds stormed the government buildings, and guards fired on them, killing dozens. Bakiyev fled south and then abroad.

An interim government under Roza Otunbayeva, the first woman to lead a Central Asian state, took over. Weeks later the south exploded in the Osh clashes. A new constitution that year made Kyrgyzstan a parliamentary republic, but later leaders pulled power back to the president, and a third uprising, in 2020, brought Sadyr Japarov to power.
sum: The 2010 Kyrgyz revolution was the uprising of April 2010 that overthrew President Kurmanbek Bakiyev of Kyrgyzstan, who had come to power in the Tulip Revolution of 2005.
